title: The Agentic AI Super Cycle
gist: Geoff Tate argues agentic AI is a 10+ year super cycle: agents already consume over half of tokens, compute needs rise orders of magnitude, hyperscaler AI capex shows 1-2 year paybacks, and capital is abundant. He expects custom silicon to pressure Nvidia after 2030 and TSMC's AI concentration to become a systemic single point of failure.

themes.theme: Scale of AI capex and macro weight

insights.claim: Data center AI capex will reach about $1 trillion this year and is projected at $3-4 trillion by 2030, against world GDP of about $123 trillion, taking AI from roughly 1% to 3% of GDP.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Sizes the spending runway for the AI hardware supply chain through 2030.

insights.claim: More than half of US GDP growth is now attributed to AI infrastructure investment, far above the roughly 7% global GDP uplift over 10 years that Goldman Sachs and McKinsey projected for generative AI.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: US growth is concentrated in AI capex, creating macro fragility if spending pauses.
insights.locator: A few years ago, Goldman Sachs

insights.claim: Eight of the world's top 10 companies by market cap are major AI players (Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, TSMC, SpaceX, Meta, Broadcom), together almost 20% of global listed market cap, and Anthropic is expected to join the top 10 later this year.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Index concentration in AI names means portfolio risk is increasingly one AI factor.

insights.claim: Nvidia is projecting about 70% revenue growth next year at huge scale, which the author treats as plausible rather than impossible.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Sets the expectation bar for the leading AI chip supplier.

insights.claim: Agentic AI is argued to be more economically impactful than generative AI and any prior industrial revolution, because over half of advanced-economy GDP is labor and over half of that is cognitive work that agents can make more productive.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: The addressable market is labor spend, not software budgets, which supports very large capex.
insights.locator: Agentic AI is much more powerful

insights.claim: The supercycle holds if three conditions are met: agentic AI has high ROI, a huge TAM, and keeps getting more powerful and cheaper; if so it is a 10+ year cycle with losers, pauses, plateaus and consolidation along the way.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Gives three testable variables to monitor for the cycle ending.

insights.claim: Even a pacing of frontier model development, as Anthropic's CEO called for, would not slow investment because safeguards require more training and, per OpenAI's CFO, existing intelligence already offers large growth opportunities.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Safety-driven pacing is not a near-term capex headwind in this view.

insights.claim: The author's conclusion is that looking out 5-10 years is hard, with key uncertainties being whether token cost falls faster than token demand rises and when a post-Transformer architecture arrives; the path could be a straight line or a roller coaster.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Acknowledges that the direction may be right while the timing and volatility are uncertain.

themes.theme: ROI and cash recovery on AI infrastructure

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley concluded in July that major hyperscalers have paths to 25-50% ROIC on GenAI investment.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Supports the argument that capex is earning returns rather than just being a bubble.

insights.claim: Google says it recovers its cash outlay for a TPU in one year and for its Axion CPU in two years, and Google Cloud's CEO said TPUs paid back twice as fast as GPUs, implying GPUs pay back in about two years, though land and building costs may be omitted.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Very short payback periods justify custom silicon and aggressive capex, but may exclude facility costs.

insights.claim: Strong chip-level paybacks are not yet lifting Google's near-term profits because it keeps raising capex faster than revenue grows.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Reported margins will lag unit economics while capex growth outpaces revenue.

insights.claim: Amazon builds data centers and racks in parallel with Trainium chips so shipments go from the end of the production line into revenue-producing operation within a couple of months, versus the serial chip-tray-rack-row approach that ties up cash longer.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Deployment speed is a hidden source of ROI advantage among hyperscalers.
insights.locator: Amazon senior vice president Peter DeSantis

insights.claim: New Street forecasts hyperscaler free cash flow bottoming in 2028 at negative 20% of revenue and turning to positive 10% by 2030, with AI cloud revenue growing almost 10x from 2026 to 2030 and exceeding non-AI cloud revenue by 2030.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Implies several years of cash burn before payoff, which matters for credit and equity timing.

insights.claim: Major AI suppliers look profitable: TSMC, Nvidia, Broadcom and Microsoft have gross margins above 60%, and Anthropic is rumored at about 80%, so valuations look reasonable given growth as long as ROIC on AI capex stays positive.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Valuation defense rests on one assumption: continued positive AI capex ROIC.

themes.theme: Token demand, agents and compute intensity

insights.claim: Cisco says agent token consumption now exceeds human GenAI token consumption (over 50% of demand) while under 2% of humans use agents as power users, so agentic tokens could grow about 50x at full power-user adoption on today's models.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Adoption headroom implies demand growth without any model improvement.

insights.claim: Goldman Sachs projects token consumption will grow 40x from mid-2026 to mid-2030.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: A concrete demand curve to compare against supply buildout.

insights.claim: Nvidia showed agentic AI is about 100x more compute-intensive than chat, even with just four agents.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Agents multiply compute per user, so usage growth is not proportional to user growth.

insights.claim: Pat Gelsinger argues AI infrastructure needs a 10,000x improvement across the stack, noting reasoning models need 10x more computation, future models 10-100x more than that, adoption is at most one tenth complete, and most enterprises are just starting.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Frames a multi-order-of-magnitude buildout rather than incremental growth.

insights.claim: Jevons paradox applies: cheaper tokens increase total consumption, as seen in GenAI growing to over a billion monthly users and over 100 million daily users, so falling cost per token raises rather than lowers compute demand.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Efficiency gains from new chips should be read as demand-expanding, not capex-reducing.

insights.claim: Google told staff it must double AI serving capacity every six months to reach 1000x in 4-5 years.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: A hyperscaler's own internal capacity target signals the supply chain pull-through.

themes.theme: Cost per token and Nvidia roadmap

insights.claim: Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 offers up to 30x better performance at high responsiveness and up to 45x lower cost per token than GB300 NVL72, with gains smaller for batch AI and largest for agentic workloads needing quick responses.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Vendor benchmarks favor agentic inference, supporting upgrade cycles.
insights.locator: Ian Buck showed the performance boost

insights.claim: Epoch.AI data shows cost per token falling about 9x per year on the simplest tasks and 900x per year on the most complex, roughly consistent with Nvidia's figures.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Deflation in token cost is extreme, so revenue per token must fall or volume must explode.

insights.claim: Nvidia plans an annual cadence: Vera Rubin Ultra next year, then Feynman, then Feynman Ultra, and Huang attributes gains mainly to networking: the GPU is the network of chips, scaling from 4 to 72 (NVL72) and soon NVL576 with optical interconnect.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Networking and optical interconnect are the key scaling levers.
insights.quote: the GPU isn’t the chip, it’s the network of chips working together
insights.locator: At the Goldman Sachs Technology Conference, Huang

insights.claim: Anthropic said in September that frontier models lead about 26% of the R&D work to build newer frontier models under human supervision, with no part currently fully autonomous.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Quantifies the self-improvement feedback loop at an early stage.

insights.claim: OpenAI has an automated research intern for tasks taking a skilled researcher days and is progressing toward an automated AI researcher by early 2028; it also took nine months to tape out its first chip, Jalapeno, using its own tools for architecture evaluation.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: AI-assisted chip design shortens custom silicon timelines, threatening incumbents' moat.

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley estimates the global knowledge-work TAM for AI at $20-30 trillion, with 13% penetration by 2033 equal to $3.2 trillion of enterprise AI spend, almost double 2030 spend, plus $30 trillion of consumer spend to be digitized with faster adoption.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Even a modest penetration assumption keeps AI capex growing into the 2030s.

insights.claim: Adoption could be much faster than large-company barriers suggest, because pacesetter companies can use hyperscaler infrastructure immediately and gain competitive advantage over less nimble rivals.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Upside risk to enterprise adoption timelines versus consensus.

insights.claim: AI infrastructure financing is abundant and oversubscribed: companies stay private longer funded by East Coast funds and Gulf sovereign wealth, and Blackstone is buying tens of billions of Google TPUs and jointly financing $500 billion of Nvidia GPUs.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Private credit and asset managers are now primary funders of compute hardware.

insights.claim: Hyperscaler capex now exceeds free cash flow, so they are issuing debt, and investors prefer Alphabet and Amazon notes over T-bills.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Leverage is rising in AI leaders, linking AI health to credit markets.

insights.claim: Every hyperscaler and frontier model maker will build its own AI compute, so GPUs face competition from custom chips; Nvidia should stay dominant through 2030 on supply chain and financial strength but be more pressured after, and may have to become more like a hyperscaler, cut prices, or sell total solutions.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Nvidia's share erosion risk is post-2030, with strategic moves already visible.
insights.locator: Every hyperscaler and frontier model maker

insights.claim: ASIC suppliers will likely be acquired and integrated by hyperscalers and frontier model makers as AI compute becomes a larger internal business.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Merchant custom-silicon vendors face vertical-integration risk or become acquisition targets.

insights.claim: TSMC builds over 90% of AI compute devices and will become majority AI, making the world economy dependent on a single point of failure, which will push hyperscalers to try Intel Foundry and Samsung for price competition and backup capacity.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Creates an opening for second-source foundries, while concentration risk stays systemic.
insights.locator: TSMC's business will become majority AI

insights.claim: Frontier training compute has grown about 4-5x annually, from roughly 2e21 FLOPs for GPT-2 to 2e25 for GPT-4, and Epoch.AI projects about 2e29 FLOPs by 2030, requiring possibly a million or more GPUs and, because training is latency-sensitive, vertical high-rise data centers.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: Cluster density needs push demand for interconnect, packaging and novel data center design.

insights.claim: TSMC's CFO says we are still in the very early stage of a megatrend, and TSMC is building numerous large fabs and advanced packaging factories to keep up as falling token cost increases compute demand.
insights.speaker: Geoff Tate
insights.so_what: The key supplier's capacity expansion signals confidence in long-run demand.
